title: Context Window
similar: LeetCode 340 Longest Substring with At Most K Distinct Characters
hints: Cheap spans stay cheap when you cut tokens off either end. What does that let you do with a left pointer?
Grow the right end one token at a time and track how many distinct ids are inside. When there are too many, what must move?
Keep a map id -> count. While the map has more than k keys, decrement the left id and erase it at zero. Record right - left + 1 after each fix-up.

wrong.reset_window.cpp: restarts the window from the new token instead of shrinking from the left
wrong.no_erase.cpp: never erases an id whose count reaches zero, so the distinct count never drops
wrong.tle_rescan.cpp: restarts a set scan at every start index (quadratic, fails the perf group)

strategy.question: Scout the statement: which plan fits n up to 2*10^5 and 'longest consecutive run with at most k distinct ids'?
options: Try every start and extend until the distinct count exceeds k
Sort the ids, then count distinct values
Slide a window: grow on the right, shrink from the left while it has too many distinct ids
Binary search the length and check every span of that length with a fresh set
strategy.why: Cheap spans stay cheap when shrunk, so one left pointer that only moves forward is enough: O(n). Trying every start is O(n^2). Sorting destroys the consecutive structure. Binary search on length works (cheapness is monotone in length) but a fresh set per span makes the check O(n*len) unless you also slide, so it is more code for no gain.
